s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of syncope with exertional fatigue in a patient with a history of heart failure and aortic valve replacement
salient_findings: Syncope without preceding signs or symptoms
Prolonged PR interval and QRS duration on ECG
key_facts: Current medications: warfarin, furosemide, metoprolol succinate, and spironolactone
ECG findings: regular sinus rhythm, prolonged PR interval, prolonged QRS duration
Echocardiogram findings: ejection fraction 28%, akinesia of middle and basal segments of inferior and inferoseptal walls
24-hour Holter monitoring: regular rhythm, mean heart rate 77 beats/min

shortlist.label: High-grade atrioventricular block
shortlist.why_kept: Prolonged PR interval and QRS duration on ECG

shortlist.label: Cardiac conduction disease
shortlist.why_kept: Prolonged PR interval and QRS duration on ECG, left axis deviation

shortlist.label: Prosthetic valve thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of aortic valve replacement and prosthetic valve thrombosis complication

shortlist.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Echocardiogram findings of ejection fraction 28% and diffuse left ventricular hypocontractility

shortlist.label: Cardiac amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of heart failure and exertional fatigue, potential for restrictive cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG findings, including a prolonged PR interval and prolonged QRS duration, are indicative of cardiac conduction disease. Additionally, the patient's history of aortic valve replacement surgery and prosthetic valve thrombosis may have contributed to the development of conduction abnormalities.

rejected.label: High-grade atrioventricular block
rejected.why: While the patient has a prolonged PR interval, there is no mention of a complete block or significant pauses on the 24-hour Holter monitoring.

rejected.label: Prosthetic valve thrombosis
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of prosthetic valve thrombosis, the current presentation and findings do not suggest an acute thrombotic event.

rejected.label: Dilated cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's echocardiogram findings of akinesia of middle and basal segments of inferior and inferoseptal walls and diffuse left ventricular hypocontractility are more suggestive of a localized wall motion abnormality rather than a globally dilated ventricle.

rejected.label: Cardiac amyloidosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the vignette to suggest cardiac amyloidosis, such as characteristic echocardiographic findings or biopsy results.
